item.text: {"text":"Recent results support text-aware item representations, but provide limited direct evidence for a lightweight text encoder trained from scratch within NextItNet. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) learns attribute-aware representations and matches user preferences to item attributes; it uses pretrained language models, so its results do not establish effectiveness under the no-pretraining constraint. [Bidirectional alignment text-embeddings (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705125003375) explores sequence–target contrastive alignment and expanded negatives. These suggest useful mechanisms, rather than directly transferable recipes. No verified exact-match 2024–2026 study emerged from this search.\n\nA plausible experiment is one jointly trained NextItNet per category: encode permitted titles and descriptions with randomly initialized token embeddings and masked mean pooling or a small text CNN; project and gate the text vector into the item-ID embedding before the existing causal dilated residual convolutions. Use the same integrated item representation for candidate scoring, optimizing everything through next-item prediction. This is an architectural inference, not a published performance claim. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supports efficient short- and long-range sequence modeling through dilated convolutions and residual blocks. Shared word parameters could help sparse items borrow statistical strength, but noisy descriptions and limited interaction supervision could erase that benefit. Compare against the corrected ID-only baseline using macro validation HR@10; retain one checkpoint per category, final-nonpadding readout, and identical training/predictor architecture. Text supplies observable product distinctions, not evidence of ownership or current intent."}
